options.B: The corticosteroid to coat the throat
options.C: The bronchodilator to open the airways
options.D: Neither, they must be mixed together first

explanation: Using the bronchodilator first opens up the air passages, allowing the subsequent corticosteroid to penetrate much deeper into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT an environmental barrier to communication?

options.A: Severe patient anxiety and panic
options.B: Distracting television volume
options.C: Loud monitor alarms and busy hallways
options.D: Lack of privacy in a crowded ward

explanation: You got it! Anxiety is an emotional or internal feeling, whereas environmental barriers are about physical surroundings like noise and crowds. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the correct compression-to-breath ratio for single-rescuer adult CPR?

options.A: 5 compressions to 1 breath
options.B: 100 compressions to 5 breaths
options.C: 30 compressions to 2 breaths
options.D: 15 compressions to 2 breaths

explanation: The golden rule for adult BLS is 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths. You'll memorize this in no time! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T6#GNS321_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which physical change is typically seen in a patient with Cushing's syndrome?

options.A: Profound skin hyperpigmentation
options.B: Moon face and a buffalo hump
options.C: Severe cold intolerance and tremors
options.D: Rapid, unexpected weight loss

explanation: Too much cortisol changes how fat is stored in the body, leading to a rounded 'moon face' and a fatty pad on the upper back known as a buffalo hump. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h4)

question: Which imaging tool is usually used first to check for fluid in the Pouch of Douglas?

options.A: Barium enema study
options.B: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.C: MRI scan
options.D: Plain abdominal X-ray

explanation: You've got this! A transvaginal ultrasound gives a clear, close-up look at pelvic structures and spots fluid pockets easily without surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T27#GNS216_U5_T27_h4)

question: A patient remembers their childhood clearly but cannot recall what they ate an hour ago. What kind of memory loss is this?

options.A: Global retrograde amnesia wiping out all past decades
options.B: Anterograde amnesia with preserved remote memory
options.C: Pure procedural amnesia affecting motor skills only
options.D: Transient global amnesia that will resolve in hours

explanation: You've got it! 'Anterograde' means trouble making *new* memories, while older childhood memories ('remote memory') stay safe in the back of the mind. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T8#GNS222_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why do misplaced endometrial implants cause ongoing pain and scarring in the pelvis?

options.A: They grow rapidly into malignant tumors within weeks
options.B: They release massive amounts of male hormones into the abdomen
options.C: They bleed during each cycle, causing local inflammation and adhesions
options.D: They destroy the nerves supplying the lower abdominal wall

explanation: Wherever these misplaced cells land, they still respond to monthly hormones by trying to 'bleed'. This trapped blood irritates nearby tissue, causing painful inflammation and sticky scar tissue. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h6)

question: When is a syringe driver most likely to be used for a patient?

options.A: When the patient refuses all forms of nursing care
options.B: When intravenous access is completely forbidden by law
options.C: When the patient needs rapid blood pressure support
options.D: When oral medications are no longer safe or possible

explanation: Exactly! If a patient cannot swallow, has severe vomiting, or is nearing the end of life, a syringe driver is a lifesaver for giving regular medications smoothly. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h2)

question: A patient tells you they are resting at home in their own bed, but they are actually sitting in a hospital ward. How would you describe this?

options.A: Normal cognitive aging changes
options.B: Disorientation to place
options.C: Impaired immediate recall memory
options.D: A defect in cranial nerve function

explanation: When a patient doesn't realize where they physically are, we document it as disorientation to place. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T4#GNS222_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is considered the gold standard imaging method for verifying the final position of an endotracheal tube?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
options.B: Computed tomography (CT) scan
options.C: Abdominal ultrasound
options.D: Chest X-ray

explanation: A chest X-ray provides definitive visual proof showing exactly how far the tube is from the tracheal bifurcation (carina). [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h5)

question: Which Nigerian agency works closely with the Ministry of Health to regulate and oversee drug standards?

options.A: NEMA
options.B: EFCC
options.C: NAFDAC
options.D: JAMB

explanation: You know this! NAFDAC is our frontline agency in Nigeria keeping fake and unsafe drugs away from our people. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is a very common cause of weakened pelvic floor muscles in women?

options.A: Vaginal childbirth
options.B: Regular aerobic exercise
options.C: Eating high-fiber foods
options.D: Drinking too much water

explanation: The stretching and hard work of vaginal delivery can tire out or stretch the pelvic floor support structures, making leaks more likely later on. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h4)

question: What fills the chest space when a patient has a hemothorax?

options.A: Air
options.B: Serous fluid
options.C: Blood
options.D: Pus

explanation: Easy and clear! 'Hemo' means blood, and 'thorax' means chest. It's blood inside the chest cavity. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which abnormal protein builds up inside the nerve cells in Pick's disease?

options.A: Tau protein
options.B: Beta-amyloid
options.C: Alpha-synuclein
options.D: Prion protein

explanation: Think of tau proteins as building blocks that go rogue and clump up inside the brain cells in Pick's disease. Knowing this pathology makes the rest of the topic much easier to master! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the main root cause of inherited degenerative diseases?

options.A: Genetic mutations passed down within families
options.B: Severe vitamin deficiencies in childhood
options.C: Bacterial infections in the nervous system
options.D: Sudden physical trauma to the brain

explanation: You've got this! These conditions happen because of changes in the genes passed down from parents, leading to gradual tissue breakdown over time. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T14#GNS222_U4_T14_h1)

question: How does the medicine lactulose help a patient with liver confusion (hepatic encephalopathy)?

options.A: By increasing blood pressure in the portal vein
options.B: By stimulating the liver to produce more albumin
options.C: By trapping ammonia in the gut and helping pass it out
options.D: By killing viruses attacking the liver cells

explanation: Lactulose makes the bowel acidic, trapping ammonia so the body can flush it out in the stool instead of letting it reach the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which type of bedpan is best to use for a patient who has a broken hip?

options.A: A standard high-backed bedpan
options.B: A rigid plastic commode chair
options.C: A fracture pan
options.D: A pediatric incontinence ring

explanation: Fracture pans are shallow, meaning you don't have to lift the patient's hips high up. This is a lifesaver for avoiding extra pain or injury when dealing with hip or pelvic bones! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h2)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for someone living with long-term Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Completely restoring lost declarative memories from childhood
options.B: Training the brain to regrow lost neurons through intense puzzles
options.C: Teaching the patient how to fabricate stories more convincingly
options.D: Maximizing remaining functional independence using environmental aids

explanation: Since memory loss sticks around, we focus on helping them stay safe and independent using daily routines, calendars, and friendly cues. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T8#GNS222_U4_T8_h8)

question: What is the greatest risk if a patient suddenly stops taking their daily anti-seizure medication?

options.A: A sudden drop in resting blood pressure
options.B: Total paralysis of the lower extremities
options.C: Severe rebound seizures or status epilepticus
options.D: Immediate permanent memory loss

explanation: Abrupt withdrawal of anticonvulsants removes the chemical brake on the brain, frequently triggering dangerous, continuous seizure activity. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h6)

question: Why must you check if two drugs are compatible before adding an IV piggyback medicine into an existing line?

options.A: Hospital pharmacy software blocks incompatible infusions anyway.
options.B: Primary fluids neutralize the therapeutic effect of all antibiotics.
options.C: Incompatible drugs can form precipitates that block the catheter.
options.D: Mismatched drugs will automatically cause severe patient hypertension.

explanation: Spot on! Mixing the wrong drugs can cause chemical reactions that turn into solid gunk, clogging the line and endangering the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T15#GNS122_U1_T15_h6)

question: Why is it important to understand cultural beliefs during palliative communication?

options.A: It prevents patients from talking about their symptoms
options.B: It allows nurses to change the patient's religious beliefs
options.C: It is required to reduce hospital medication costs
options.D: It helps tailor care discussions to respect family traditions and elders

explanation: Culture shapes how families view illness and make decisions, especially with elders involved. Respecting this makes our nursing care truly compassionate. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why is precise regional terminology crucial for nursing documentation?

options.A: It ensures clear tracking of wound healing and prevents charting errors
options.B: It eliminates the need for taking vital signs during a physical check
options.C: It guarantees that patients will understand their own discharge summaries
options.D: It reduces the total number of words nurses need to type in a shift

explanation: Using specific anatomical regions lets every nurse reading the chart know the exact location and progress of an injury. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which condition causes facial swelling, neck vein bulging, and trouble breathing due to a blocked major vein?

options.A: Spinal Cord Compression
options.B: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome
options.C: Febrile Neutropenia
options.D: Tumor Lysis Syndrome

explanation: When a tumor presses on the superior vena cava, blood gets backed up in the upper body, causing that distinct facial swelling. Spotting this makes you a sharp nurse! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h6)

question: What happens to the body when the bone marrow fails to produce enough blood cells?

options.A: Nerve impulse transmission and muscle contraction stop
options.B: Oxygen delivery, immune defense, and clotting all suffer
options.C: Nutrient digestion and waste filtration fail completely
options.D: Hormone production and electrolyte balance drop rapidly

explanation: Think of blood as your body's vital transport system! Its cells carry oxygen to keep you energized, fight off germs, and stop bleeding when you get a cut. When marrow fails, all three jobs take a hit. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T14#GNS311_U2_T14_h1)

question: A client gets mild sedation to stay calm during a long MRI. What must the nurse watch most closely?

options.A: Breathing rate and oxygen levels
options.B: Bowel sounds in all four abdominal areas
options.C: The exact room temperature
options.D: How fast the client can walk afterward

explanation: Sedatives can slow down breathing, so keeping an eye on the patient's respiratory rate and oxygen is top priority! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T8#GNS222_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is the main focus of gerontology?

options.A: The manufacturing of mobility aids for the elderly
options.B: The surgical treatment of age-related diseases
options.C: The management of hospital finances for seniors
options.D: The study of the aging process and older adults

explanation: Gerontology is a broad scientific field that examines physical, mental, and social aspects of aging. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is a crucial teaching point for someone prescribed an epinephrine auto-injector for severe allergies?

options.A: Keep the device stored inside a kitchen refrigerator at all times
options.B: Demonstrate how to self-administer the device into the outer thigh and call emergency services
options.C: Use the auto-injector only after taking oral antihistamines first
options.D: Replace the device once every ten years regardless of expiration date

explanation: Make sure your patient knows how to jab that auto-injector firmly into their outer thigh, and remind them to always call for emergency help right after! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h8)

question: You are getting ready to put a stockinette on a patient's lower leg that has a small healing sore. What is the best first step for that wound?

options.A: Scrub the ulcer vigorously with iodine until it stops bleeding
options.B: Leave the wound completely uncovered so it can breathe under the cast
options.C: Apply antibiotic ointment directly to the stockinette fabric
options.D: Cover the ulcer with a sterile dressing before putting on the stockinette

explanation: Standard stockinettes are clean, but not sterile! Always cover open wounds with a sterile dressing first to keep your patient safe. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which sign around a surgical drain insertion site tells you an infection might be starting?

options.A: Normal skin color with slight firmness around the tube
options.B: Clear pink fluid on a dry, intact outer gauze
options.C: Foul-smelling pus and surrounding skin redness
options.D: A small drop of dried blood near the stitches

explanation: Spot on! Redness, warmth, swelling, and foul-smelling pus are classic signs that bacteria are multiplying. Time to alert the team! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h4)

question: Which of these situations calls for immediate surgery in genitourinary trauma?

options.A: Hemodynamic instability and active internal bleeding
options.B: A small bruise on the skin over the lower ribs
options.C: Mild hematuria that clears up within two hours
options.D: Anxiety about the hospital environment

explanation: If a patient's vital signs are crashing because of ongoing internal bleeding, surgery is needed right away to stop the leak. Safety first! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h7)

question: What is the most dangerous situation where a barium enema must NEVER be done?

options.A: Well-controlled high blood pressure
options.B: Suspected or known tear (perforation) in the gut
options.C: Mild internal piles without bleeding
options.D: A history of mild, ongoing constipation

explanation: If barium leaks out through a hole in the bowel, it causes severe and dangerous inflammation inside the abdomen. Safety first! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h3)

question: A patient says, 'I cannot be healthy because I am too weak to go to work and look after my children.' Which health model are they using?

options.A: Clinical model
options.B: Role performance model
options.C: Eudaimonistic model
options.D: Biological germ model

explanation: Spot on! This model measures health by whether a person can successfully carry out their daily family and job responsibilities. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why do we prefer a closed bladder irrigation system over an open one?

options.A: It allows the nurse to bypass the need for a physician order
options.B: It lowers the risk of introducing bacteria into the bladder
options.C: It prevents the patient from feeling any bladder spasms at all
options.D: It requires much less total fluid volume over twenty-four hours

explanation: Keeping everything connected means fewer germs can slip inside, which helps your patient avoid a nasty UTI. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T23#GNS212_U1_T23_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of disrupted ovarian cycles?

options.A: Severe physical or emotional stress
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Extreme weight loss or eating disorders
options.D: Drinking adequate daily water

explanation: Normal fluid intake supports health but does not disrupt the delicate hormonal axis that controls ovulation, unlike severe stress, weight loss, or disease states. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why are the testicles located outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To keep sperm production at a cooler temperature than body core temperature
options.B: To protect the delicate sperm cells from harsh digestive enzymes
options.C: To make it easier for the body to produce testosterone hormones
options.D: To increase the pressure needed for proper ejaculation

explanation: Sperm production requires a slightly cooler environment than internal body temperature to develop properly. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h2)

question: How does pelvic floor physical therapy help treat genito-pelvic pain?

options.A: It removes scar tissue from previous vaginal surgeries
options.B: It permanently blocks nerve signals to the clitoris
options.C: It increases systemic testosterone production instantly
options.D: It relaxes and conditions hypertonic pelvic muscles

explanation: Spot on! When pelvic muscles are overworked and too tight (hypertonic), physical therapy teaches the patient how to consciously relax and lengthen them. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T25#GNS312_U1_T25_h7)

question: A nurse cares for a patient with a drug-resistant wound infection. Which principle guides safe nursing care?

options.A: Treating all patient blood and body fluids as infectious using standard precautions
options.B: Reusing medical equipment between patients if it looks visually clean
options.C: Stopping all hand hygiene once gloves are removed from the hands
options.D: Assuming infection control is only necessary if the patient shows a high fever

explanation: Standard precautions require treating all bodily fluids as potentially infectious to protect against both known and unknown pathogens. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h8)

question: What is the main difference between illness and disease?

options.A: Illness is how the person feels and experiences their sickness, while disease is the medical pathology
options.B: Illness can only be diagnosed with lab tests, while disease is purely psychological
options.C: Disease is a subjective feeling, whereas illness is an objective medical label
options.D: There is no practical difference between the two terms in nursing

explanation: Illness is subjective and personal, while disease is the clinical pathology diagnosed by a doctor. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h2)

question: How should you position a patient right after a craniotomy surgery to help keep intracranial pressure down?

options.A: Sitting upright at a 90-degree angle
options.B: Flat on the back with feet raised high
options.C: Head elevated 30 to 45 degrees
options.D: Lying flat on the operative side

explanation: Excellent clinical thinking! Elevating the head of the bed helps blood flow smoothly out of the head (venous return), preventing fluid backup and keeping pressure low. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h6)

question: Which of these is a common natural chemical preservative?

options.A: Sodium benzoate
options.B: Artificial nitrate
options.C: Common salt
options.D: Sulfur dioxide

explanation: Salt has been trusted for centuries to draw out moisture and stop bacteria dead in their tracks. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T011#GNS227_U3_T011_h5)

question: Which gland releases cortisol when signaled by the pituitary gland during stress?

options.A: Adrenal cortex
options.B: Thyroid gland
options.C: Pineal gland
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: The outer layer of your adrenal glands (right above your kidneys) is called the adrenal cortex, and it pumps out cortisol to help you handle stress. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T8#GNS123_U1_T8_h2)

question: What do we mean by 'gender norms'?

options.A: Genetic markers inherited from parents
options.B: Medical guidelines for reproductive health
options.C: Fixed biological limits of the human body
options.D: Societal rules dictating expected behaviors

explanation: Great job! Gender norms are simply the unwritten rules or cultural standards that society uses to guide how men and women 'should' act. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T3#GNS312_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why is it a must to check a patient's blood glucose level before injecting the PET tracer?

options.C: High blood sugar competes with the tracer and ruins the image quality.
options.D: Elevated glucose levels neutralize the radioactivity of the tracer.

explanation: Spot on! If there is too much normal sugar in the blood, the cells will eat that instead of our FDG tracer, and the scan pictures will turn out blurry or misleading. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h4)

question: What is the primary cause of tissue damage in a pressure sore?

options.A: Prolonged pressure cutting off blood supply
options.B: Excessive moisture from heavy sweating
options.C: Bacterial infection of the sweat glands
options.D: Allergic reaction to hospital bedsheets

explanation: Pressure sores form when constant external pressure stops blood flow to the skin and deep tissues, causing them to die from lack of oxygen. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h1)

question: Which body system is most commonly involved when studying paroxysmal disorders like epilepsy?

options.A: The renal filtration system
options.B: The gastrointestinal tract
options.C: The integumentary system
options.D: The central nervous system

explanation: Most classic paroxysmal disorders, such as seizures, originate from sudden electrical disruptions in the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h1)

question: A patient goes home after treatment for a bleeding gastric ulcer. Which symptom should they report to the nurse immediately?

options.A: Mild gas after eating vegetables
options.B: A slight increase in morning appetite
options.C: Passing dark, tarry stools
options.D: Occasional burping after drinking water

explanation: Well done! Black, tarry stools mean there is digested blood coming from higher up in the gut, which can be a sign of dangerous bleeding. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h7)

question: What is the key job of the special fluid called surfactant in your lungs?

options.A: To reduce surface tension and prevent alveolar collapse
options.B: To bind oxygen molecules directly for transport
options.C: To moisten the trachea and primary bronchi
options.D: To trap dust and bacteria entering the deep lungs

explanation: Brilliant! Surfactant keeps the tiny air sacs from sticking together and collapsing on themselves when you breathe out. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the most effective public health strategy for preventing obstetric fistulae in communities?

options.A: Improving access to skilled birth attendants and emergency obstetric care
options.B: Administering daily vitamin supplements during the third trimester
options.C: Providing free diapers to all women living in rural communities
options.D: Encouraging women to give birth at home without professional assistance

explanation: You nailed it! Getting help quickly during difficult labour prevents the prolonged pressure that causes fistulas. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h6)

question: Why do doctors avoid doing a direct needle biopsy of a heart mass?

options.A: It destroys all the electrical conduction pathways in the heart
options.B: It carries a high risk of breaking off pieces of the tumour to cause an embolism
options.C: It is completely impossible to insert any catheter into the heart chambers
options.D: It causes the heart to permanently stop beating within seconds

explanation: Poke a fragile heart tumour with a needle, and pieces might break off and travel through the bloodstream to cause a stroke! Safety first in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T8#GNS213_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is keeping a steady level of calcium in your body so important for daily function?

options.A: It prevents the pancreas from producing too much digestive acid.
options.B: It is required for proper nerve conduction and muscle contraction.
options.C: It maintains the normal filtering pressure inside the liver lobules.
options.D: It directly controls the total volume of circulating red blood cells.

explanation: Calcium is essential for sending nerve signals and making your muscles move smoothly. Without it, your nerves and muscles simply cannot function right! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T11#GNS222_U2_T11_h2)

question: A patient with unsteady balance and dizziness is admitted to the medical ward. What is the most immediate safety risk to prevent?

options.A: A wrong-site surgical procedure
options.B: A severe hospital-acquired infection
options.C: A physical fall leading to injury
options.D: An accidental medication overdose

explanation: Unsteadiness and dizziness directly increase the likelihood of slips and falls, making fall precautions the priority intervention for this patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is the main difference between a bone marrow aspiration and a bone marrow biopsy?

options.A: Biopsy checks cell maturity, while aspiration checks bone strength
options.B: Biopsy uses arm veins, while aspiration uses the sternum
options.C: Aspiration needs general anaesthesia, but biopsy does not
options.D: Aspiration takes liquid, while a biopsy takes a solid piece of tissue

explanation: Think of aspiration as taking a fluid sample of the marrow, while a biopsy takes a tiny solid cylinder of bone and marrow to check its structure. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h4)

question: Your patient suddenly gasps and feels dizzy halfway through draining fluid. What should you do first?

options.A: Document the total amount of fluid drained so far
options.B: Notify the provider immediately and stop the drainage
options.C: Administer the prescribed oral pain medication right away
options.D: Ask the patient to sit up straight and take deep breaths

explanation: Safety first! Sudden dizziness or coughing can mean a rapid fluid shift or a lung issue, so pause the procedure and alert the doctor right away. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h4)

question: How wide is the standard unsterile border around a sterile drape or package wrapper?

options.A: Six inches
options.B: Three inches
options.C: One inch
options.D: Twelve inches

explanation: That outer one-inch edge of any sterile wrap is considered touched and unsterile. Good rule of thumb to always remember! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h4)

question: What do we mean by 'happy hypoxemia' in COVID-19 care?

options.A: Feeling overly energetic despite severe viral fatigue and muscle aches
options.B: Experiencing extreme chest pain while maintaining normal oxygen levels
options.C: Showing high fever and cough while blood pressure remains stable
options.D: Having dangerously low blood oxygen without feeling short of breath

question: What is the main purpose of United Nations packaging requirements in healthcare?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of shipping medical laboratory supplies
options.B: To speed up the delivery time of routine blood test results
options.C: To ensure all medical specimens look identical to couriers
options.D: To prevent leaks and spills of hazardous materials during transit

explanation: These international rules are designed specifically to contain dangerous biological or chemical contents safely even if the outer box is dropped or crushed. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h1)

question: How does social stigma make the problem of unsafe abortions even worse?

options.A: It forces women to hide their condition and delay seeking safe help
options.B: It prevents healthcare workers from learning basic nursing skills
options.C: It causes severe hormonal imbalances that mimic pregnancy complications
options.D: It directly reduces the availability of surgical equipment in hospitals

explanation: Spot on. Fear of judgment and shame makes patients wait too long or use dangerous home remedies instead of coming to us for safe care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h2)

question: What is a major nursing priority right after a patient has heart valve surgery for endocarditis?

options.A: Stopping all antibiotic medications once the patient leaves the operating room
options.B: Encouraging immediate heavy physical exercise to strengthen the heart muscle
options.C: Restricting fluid intake completely to prevent any swelling
options.D: Monitoring closely for signs of infection and evaluating neurological status for emboli

explanation: Great nursing care here means staying alert! We watch for any lingering infection and check the patient's brain function (neurological status) to catch any loose clots early. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of a vulvovaginal yeast infection (candidiasis)?

options.A: Yellow-green, frothy discharge with strawberry spots
options.B: Thick, white, cottage-cheese-like discharge with intense itching
options.C: Thin, gray-white discharge with a strong fishy odor
options.D: Clear, watery discharge with severe lower abdominal pain

explanation: Spot on! Yeast infections are famous for that thick, white discharge and relentless itching, without a fishy smell. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of tracking indicators in a PAC monitoring and evaluation system?

explanation: Stroke weakness can make throat muscles sluggish, meaning food or water can easily slip down the 'wrong pipe' into the lungs instead of the belly. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h7)

question: What is a key nursing duty when checking a pregnant patient's skin?

options.A: Differentiating harmless body changes from serious medical conditions
options.B: Telling the patient to ignore any skin changes until after delivery
options.C: Reporting all common stretch marks to the primary surgeon
options.D: Prescribing strong steroid creams to cure all rashes instantly

explanation: You are the frontline! Knowing the difference between normal pregnancy glow-ups and warning signs like cholestasis makes you an awesome nurse. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h7)

question: Why must nurses specifically ask patients about over-the-counter painkillers during a medication review?

options.A: Patients often do not consider non-prescription drugs as 'real' medications to report
options.B: Non-prescription drugs completely cure all forms of arthritis
options.C: Over-the-counter drugs have no side effects on bones or joints
options.D: Patients are legally prohibited from taking pain relievers at home

explanation: Spot-on! Patients often forget to mention everyday painkillers they buy over the counter, even though they can cause side effects or interact with other drugs. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T2#GNS222_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following describes a key difference between screening tests and diagnostic tests in prenatal care?

options.A: Screening tests estimate risk, while diagnostic tests confirm a condition
options.B: Diagnostic tests are performed on every single pregnant woman
options.C: Screening tests are only done after birth
options.D: Screening tests use surgery, while diagnostic tests are painless

explanation: Screening tests only show the probability or risk of a disorder, whereas diagnostic tests provide a definitive diagnosis. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h4)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of left-sided heart failure?

options.A: Enlarged and tender liver
options.B: Shortness of breath and crackles in the lungs
options.C: Visible bulging of the neck veins
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: When the left side of the heart struggles, blood backs up into the lungs, causing fluid buildup, breathlessness, and lung crackles. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h7)

question: Why must a nurse maintain neutrality when counseling patients about genetic risks?

options.A: To allow patients to make their own choices based on personal values
options.B: To prevent patients from asking questions about their family
options.C: To prove that genetics has no real impact on health
options.D: To ensure the hospital avoids paying for laboratory tests

explanation: Reproductive decisions are deeply personal; nurses must guide without imposing personal beliefs or forcing specific choices. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h5)

question: Which lab test is a key indicator that cells are lacking oxygen and relying on backup energy pathways?

options.A: Blood lactate level
options.B: Serum sodium level
options.C: Total serum protein
options.D: Platelet count

explanation: Lactate builds up like exhaust smoke when cells are starved of oxygen and forced into anaerobic metabolism. Checking blood lactate is a quick way to see how severe the tissue oxygen shortage is. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h5)

question: Which finding around a skeletal traction pin site means you need to call the doctor right away?

options.A: A small amount of clear dried crust around the metal entry point
options.B: The metal pin is visibly loose or wobbling
options.C: Mild skin redness close to the pin
options.D: Clear fluid drainage during the first day

explanation: You're doing great! Pins need to stay rock-solid in the bone. A loose pin messes up the whole traction setup and always needs a doctor's attention. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T7#GNS221_U1_T7_h4)

question: Before you start collecting data for a community diagnosis, what is usually the very first step?

options.A: Securing administrative clearance and mobilizing stakeholders
options.B: Building a permanent health clinic building
options.C: Writing the final evaluation report for the ministry
options.D: Treating all sick children with antibiotics

explanation: You always want to respect local authority! Getting permission and greeting community leaders comes first before marching in with clipboards. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T2#GNS124_U3_T2_h4)

question: How many major components typically make up a comprehensive neurological assessment?

options.A: Eight
options.B: Twelve
options.C: Two
options.D: Five

explanation: The standard exam covers mental status, cranial nerves, motor system, sensory system, and reflexes. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the main goal of a surgical bypass graft for a blocked leg artery?

options.A: To create a detour route around a blocked section of an artery
options.B: To widen a narrowed vein using a tiny wire mesh tube
options.C: To completely cut off blood flow to the lower leg
options.D: To dissolve old fatty buildup inside the tiny capillaries

explanation: Just like a road bypass helps cars drive around road construction, a surgical graft uses a healthy vessel tube to reroute blood past the blockage! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T11#GNS213_U1_T11_h5)

question: You notice a family member pressuring a heavily sedated patient to sign a document. What is your best first step as an advocate?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately from the ward
options.B: Ignore it because family financial matters are none of your business
options.C: Intervene to stop the activity and notify the nurse-in-charge or security
options.D: Help the family member hold the pen to finish quickly

explanation: Spot on! Protecting vulnerable, incapacitated patients from exploitation is a core part of your duty as a nurse. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do right after a shock is delivered?

options.A: Resume chest compressions right away
options.B: Administer a routine dose of IV atropine
options.C: Draw blood samples for arterial blood gas analysis
options.D: Check the carotid pulse for up to one minute

explanation: Don't pause to check for a pulse immediately! Modern resuscitation rules tell us to jump right back into chest compressions to keep blood flowing. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T17#GNS213_U1_T17_h5)

question: A pregnant woman at 36 weeks comes in with a fully infibulated Type III FGM scar. What is the best clinical approach?

options.A: Advise her to deliver completely unassisted at home
options.B: Plan for an antenatal or intrapartum defibulation procedure
options.C: Wait until pushing begins without any clinical preparation
options.D: Perform an immediate emergency hysterectomy

explanation: You nailed it! Planning ahead for defibulation lets the birth canal open safely before or during labor, preventing severe tears and fetal distress. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h6)

question: What does a pale inner eyelid or pale nail bed usually point to?

options.A: High blood pressure
options.B: Dehydration
options.C: Anaemia
options.D: An infection

explanation: Paleness in the mucous membranes and nails is a classic sign that the red blood cell count or haemoglobin is low, which we call anaemia. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h2)
